messages.subject: MSstatsPTM site collapse
parts:
Dear MSstatsPTM developer team,

Could you please point me towards the correct passage of the documentation / the MSstatsPTM publication or could you please briefly explain how site collapsed output has to be interpreted?

More specifically I get this (adjusted) output:

434 A0A0G2L8I2_T645
435 A0A0G2L974
436 A0A0G2L974_S1468

what does it mean if there is no PTM site reported in the adjusted table as for line 435 in the example above? I do not see this behaviour for all proteins.


186 A0A0G2KSU4_S579
187 A0A0G2KSU4_S579_S597

How can this be interpreted in layman's terms? Is the 186th two side comparison done after collapsing all quantities which definitely map to S579 and the 187th two side comparison is separately performed for all quantities which can be collapsed to either S579 or S597 and therefore MSstats says that it could be either one of them? Or that both are modified at the same time and MSstats is absolutely sure that they are both mofified at the same time?

Any help would be appreciated.

Kind Regards and thank you for your amazing tools!
Klemens

messages.author: 13904eb0f06097b0
messages.subject: Re: MSstatsPTM site collapse
parts:
Hi Klemens,

The unmodified site A0A0G2L974 is most likely there because it was in the PTM dataset before modeling. I.E. MSstatsPTM will model all the unique names in the "Protein" column that goes into the modeling function. It should not be there and is a result of the upstream data processing leaving in unmodified peptides.

In terms of multiple modification sites, MSstatsPTM assumes the identified sites the user uploads are correct. It does not do any site validation or localization. In your case there are two separate models, one for the single modification site S579 and one for the doubly modified S579 and S597. We use features with only the single modification S579 in the single modification model and use only features with both S579 and S597 in the doubly modified model. We do not try to parse out the effect of individual PTMs at this time.

I hope this makes sense.

Devon

Hi Klemens,

The unmodified site A0A0G2L974 is most likely there because it was in the PTM dataset before modeling. I.E. MSstatsPTM will model all the unique names in the "Protein" column that goes into the modeling function. It should not be there and is a result of the upstream data processing leaving in unmodified peptides.

In terms of multiple modification sites, MSstatsPTM assumes the identified sites the user uploads are correct. It does not do any site validation or localization. In your case there are two separate models, one for the single modification site S579 and one for the doubly modified S579 and S597. We use features with only the single modification S579 in the single modification model and use only features with both S579 and S597 in the doubly modified model. We do not try to parse out the effect of individual PTMs at this time.

I hope this makes sense.

Devon
